acceptance: RUBRIC 1: G1 simulation table and G2 A/B table in the PR body, with run ids
RUBRIC 2: partition tests cover group conservation and no split groups; mutation that splits a group fails a test
RUBRIC 3: a post-merge trunk run is green with grouped shards (recorded here)
RUBRIC 4: if G2 fails, PR closed and decision recorded; item finished with that outcome only if the user agrees, else left open
context:
ci-rebalance-medium-shards holds the earlier balance measurements; keep them comparable.

COMMON GUARDRAILS (apply to every long-test item; violating any is a stop)
C1 Coverage parity: for every changed, merged or deleted test, record the executed lines under benchbox/, scripts/ and _project/ (coverage API or pytest-cov, COVERAGE_CORE=sysmon, run under pytest) before and after on the affected tests. Every line lost must be executed by another named test in the same or a faster tier (show it), or be listed with a reason in the PR body. No unexplained loss.
C2 Mutation proof: any replaced or merged test, and any surviving test that is claimed to cover a deleted one, must fail on a deliberate throwaway break of the property it verifies. Record each mutation and result; never commit them; revert and confirm git status before committing.
C3 No green by weakening: no removed or loosened assertions (except deleting a whole duplicate test under C1/C2), no skip/xfail, no raised timeouts, no tier or marker moves unless this item's decision gate allows it, no mocking of the behaviour under test.
C4 Scope: change only the files this item names. Product code changes only where the item says so. No data-baseline, generator or known-divergence list changes unless named.
C5 Honest timing: label every number CI (named run) or local. Claim savings only from CI junit of a named post-change run against the baseline p95 in tests/fixtures/medium_shard_durations.json (run 39538637499). Report what is unverified.
C6 Repository process: make worktree-create with a fix/ branch, make agent-write-preflight, explicit git add paths, ruff, make comment-policy-check (no explanatory comments or docstrings), the code review action as self-review before make pr-open, oracle review, arm only on the exact head with every required check green, no attribution trailers, durable text without session or tracker labels. Do not edit PR title or body after CI starts unless needed (use make pr-rerun to retry CI).
C7 Id bookkeeping: list every new, renamed or deleted test node id in the PR body; they have no history in the coverage map or medium_shard_durations.json until item longtest-16 refreshes them.
C8 Selection impact: state whether the change alters which lines a test executes (scale change, subprocess to in-process, merge), and therefore which PRs select it and its weight in the 900 s selection estimate.
C9 Evidence durability: put the coverage diff summary, mutation table and CI timing table in the PR body (not only /tmp).
C10 Stop rule: if a decision gate fails or evidence contradicts the plan, do not improvise a different design; record the finding in this item's context and leave the item open (or blocked) with the next action.
description:
PROBLEM: module and class fixtures (Spark sessions, live canary collections, SSB and TPC-H builds, TPC-DS draws, OBT data) are rebuilt on every xdist worker and every shard that runs one of a module's tests, because shards split tests by node id (scripts/release_canary_sharding.py partition_node_ids, now duration-weighted) and each shard runs -n 5 with xdist's default load distribution; the xdist_group("pyspark") marker in tests/unit/platforms/pyspark/test_pyspark_sql_smoke.py does nothing because CI never passes --dist loadgroup. junit then charges the rebuild to the first test on each worker, which inflates medium_shard_durations.json and the 900 s selection estimate.

CHANGE:
1. Partitioner: assign whole groups (default group = test module; explicit xdist_group marks may join modules, e.g. all Spark modules) to shards, longest group first, using summed durations; keep the durations digest binding and evidence checks; round-robin path unchanged when no durations are given.
2. Workflows: run medium shards with --dist loadgroup (ci.yml, trunk.yml, trunk-coverage.yml, test.yml medium steps) and mark Spark modules with one xdist_group.
3. Durations: charge setup to the module (sum per module) when building weights, so a module's first test is not weighted as if it were the module.

DECISION GATES:
G1 Simulation first: with the current durations, report predicted per-shard sums for module-grouped vs current split; continue only if the predicted max/mean stays at or below 1.10.
G2 A/B on CI: run the PR's medium tier at least twice; compare each shard's wall time and the summed test time with two named recent develop-based PR runs. Merge only if the slowest shard and summed time both improve; otherwise close the PR and record the numbers and the decision in this item (C10).
G3 Evidence: verify-medium still proves exact coverage of the collection; all partition and workflow tests pass; add tests for group assignment (conservation, no group split across shards, balance bound).
G4 Soundness path: oracle review mandatory; trunk and release workflows change too, so check one trunk run after merge and record it.
